question: Two equal charges $+3.0\ \mu\text{C}$ each are kept $40\text{ cm}$ apart in air. Determine the electric field and electric potential at the midpoint between them. Also calculate the electrostatic potential energy of the system. Explain why the electric field and potential behave differently at the midpoint.

options.A: At the midpoint, $E=2.7\times10^5\text{ N C}^{-1}$, $V=0$, and $U=0.2025\text{ J}$ because field and potential are both vectors.
options.B: At the midpoint, $E=0$, $V=0$, and $U=0$ because equal charges cancel all effects.
options.C: At the midpoint, $E=0$, $V=1.35\times10^5\text{ V}$, and $U=0.10125\text{ J}$.
options.D: At the midpoint, the electric fields due to equal positive charges are equal and opposite, so $E=0$. Potentials add as scalars: $V=2\dfrac{kq}{0.20}=2.7\times10^5\text{ V}$. The system energy is $U=\dfrac{kq^2}{0.40}=0.2025\text{ J}$. Field cancels because it is a vector, while potential adds because it is a scalar.
